jobDescription: A building society reconciles card, faster-payment and direct-debit flows against its ledger every day. The reconciliation team writes Kotlin services that match payment records, works with payments operations on unmatched items and releases under the society's change-management controls. The team is about to redesign its matching engine and wants an engineer who has led the design and delivery of a reconciliation or ledger change, owning its technical decisions. The team has five engineers and a principal engineer and reports to the head of payments technology; releases follow the society's change calendar, and operations staff join a daily call on unmatched items.
requirements: Develops reconciliation services in Kotlin or Java.
Writes automated tests and reviews other engineers' code.
Has led the design and delivery of a reconciliation or ledger change, owning the technical decisions.
Works with operations staff to investigate unmatched items.
Releases changes under the change-management process.

evidence.text: Software engineer on the payments reconciliation team at Marlow & Pike Building Society from October 2021 to July 2024, working on the services that match card and faster-payment records against the ledger.
Implemented the matching rules for returned faster payments in the Kotlin reconciliation service, building to the design the team's principal engineer had agreed.
Wrote unit and integration tests for the matching engine, with fixtures built from anonymised return files, and reviewed pull requests from two other engineers.

Joined the daily break-review call with payments operations, investigating unmatched items and raising defects where a matching rule was wrong, then retesting each fix against the previous day's file.
Prepared release notes and change tickets for the reconciliation service; each release was approved by the change manager before deployment in the agreed change window.
Work sample: an excerpt from the matching-engine repository showing the candidate's pull request for returned faster payments, the principal engineer's review comments and the merged diff.

Reference call notes (informal, a former teammate on the reconciliation team): called the candidate 'the go-to person for the whole reconciliation rebuild' and said the principal engineer 'just signed off whatever the candidate decided'.
HR verification note: employment dates (October 2021 to July 2024) and the job title Software Engineer were checked against the employment letter from Marlow & Pike Building Society.

propositions.text: The candidate implemented the matching rules for returned faster payments in the Kotlin reconciliation service, building to the principal engineer's design.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the work and the design boundary, and the pull request shows the principal engineer's review.

propositions.text: The candidate prepared release notes and change tickets for the reconciliation service, with each release approved by the change manager.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the release work and the approval control.

propositions.text: The candidate led the reconciliation rebuild and made its technical decisions.
propositions.rationale: The claim rests on a former teammate's informal characterisation, which is an impression and second-hand comment about another person's approvals; the resume and the pull request show the candidate building to the principal engineer's design under review.

signatures: go-to person for the whole reconciliation rebuild
signed off whatever the candidate decided

gold.expectedGap: The sources document implementation of matching rules to an agreed design; leading the design or owning the technical decisions is not documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the matching-rule implementation, tests, reviews, break investigations and release work; the teammate's remarks are impressions and do not establish decision authority.
followUpTargets: Ask which technical decisions in the matching engine the candidate made personally and which the principal engineer made or approved.
